description: REQ-108's repayment-verification mechanism never de-duplicates by transaction hash, either within a SINGLE loan's own partial-repayment accumulation or ACROSS different loan_ids. REQ-108's own EARS text (lines 940-942) specifies: '`value` (converted to USD) summed with any PRIOR verified partial repayments for this SAME `loan_id` reaches at least `total_due_usd`' -- this literally instructs the implementer to take a newly-claimed transaction's own value and ADD it to the running sum of prior verified partial repayments, with NO requirement anywhere (not in the EARS text, not in the four Edge Cases, lines 968-982, not in the six Acceptance Criteria, lines 984-1008) that the NEWLY-claimed `txHash` must differ from every `txHash` ALREADY credited toward this SAME `loan_id` (or any other `loan_id`). Because `verifyRepayment`'s own three checks -- (a) receipt success + finalized block, (b) exact `to`/`from` topic-equality, (c) `value` reaching `total_due_usd` when summed with priors -- are satisfied identically whether the caller supplies a genuinely NEW transaction or RESUBMITS a txHash that was already verified and credited moments earlier, an implementer following this EARS text verbatim would build a repayment-verification function that can be invoked repeatedly with the SAME real, valid, finalized `txHash` and would credit that SAME on-chain value again each time, indefinitely, until the cumulative (fraudulently inflated) sum crosses `total_due_usd` and the loan is marked `'repaid'` -- despite the borrower having sent only ONE real payment. The SAME gap also enables a cross-loan replay: a borrower who genuinely repaid an EARLIER loan (loan_id A) with a real, finalized transaction to the SAME lender could, when a LATER loan (loan_id B) is issued to that same borrower/lender pair, resubmit loan A's ALREADY-CREDITED `txHash` as 'proof' of repayment toward loan B -- `verifyRepayment`'s own three checks would pass identically (the transaction is real, finalized, and its `from`/`to` still match), since nothing in the ledger schema (`loan_id`/`lender_id`/`borrower_id`/`principal_usd`/`repaid_usd`/`total_due_usd`/`status`/`on_time`/`issued_ms`/`due_ms`, as described piecemeal throughout the spec) records 'which loan_id(s) has this specific txHash already been credited toward,' and no Acceptance Criterion tests this. This directly undermines REQ-108's own stated principle ('never accepted from either party's own self-report alone,' line 907) and REQ-111's money-safety-invariant framing: the on-chain event's genuineness is correctly re-verified, but its UNIQUENESS/one-time-use across the entire ledger is never enforced, so a single real transfer can be credited an unbounded number of times.

evidence.snippet: value (converted to USD) summed with any PRIOR verified partial repayments for this SAME loan_id reaches at least total_due_usd (REQ-104). Verification NEVER trusts the RPC's own server-side eth_getLogs/filter result for this money invariant ... [Acceptance Criteria] A fixture with a partial-then-full repayment (two transactions summing to total_due_usd) correctly transitions the loan from active ... to repaid.

crossCheck.note: PROP-108b/PROP-108c's own fixtures (line 112-113) only ever exercise TWO DIFFERENT transaction fixtures summing to total_due_usd -- neither PROP-108b, PROP-108c, nor any other of the 43 proof obligations in this document tests resubmission of an ALREADY-credited txHash (same loan_id or a different one). No `usedTxHashes`/`consumedTxHash` field or check appears anywhere in the ledger schema described throughout behavioral-spec.md.
